name: Mesmerist — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Mesmerist from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Mesmerist" but are not part of the Mesmerist entry, which is unchanged. Sources named on the page for these sections: PPC:OO.

Sensory Blank (3pp): The subject of this trick has difficulty focusing on the mesmerist with their senses. Each time they do they seem to slide right past or through them. The mesmerist is treated as having the effects of the spell imperceptibility* against the target for 1 round per mesmerist level. However, unlike the spell, this invisibility is not affected by invisibility purge or see invisibility, nor is it impacted by spells that outline their form, though true sight will allow the subject to see the mesmerist normally. This is because the trick causes their attention to shift elsewhere whenever their senses are focused on the mesmerist. Like the spell imperceptibility this trick will end early if the mesmerist takes direct hostile action against the subject. Source LG:LM

Greater Sensory Blank (3pp): This trick acts like sensory blank except that it does not end early if the mesmerist takes direct hostile action against the subject similar to the spell greater imperceptibility. [Source]

His stare penalty increases by 2.

Devilbane Gazes

Source PPC:OO

Some mesmerists have refined their hypnotic stares to include a suite of gaze attacks useful for negotiating with or undermining outsiders.

Devilbane gazes can be selected beginning at 3rd level as options for the mesmerist’s bold stare improvements. They tend to be more limited in their scope than standard bold stare improvements, but cut to the core of an outsider’s being. When a devilbane gaze is used against a creature with the outsider type, double the hypnotic stare penalty applied by the devilbane gaze improvement (but not the Will save penalty the original hypnotic stare imposes).

Despite their moniker, devilbane gazes affect all outsiders equally well.
